hens_rule_text: Up to 6 hens allowed in the backyard of a detached single-family home on a lot of half an acre or less, under Arizona state law; the city cannot ban this even though its own older zoning code once limited chicken-keeping to agricultural and suburban-residential zones.
permit_notes: No city permit found; the state law sets the baseline right to keep up to 6 hens.
setback_notes: State law lets cities require the coop in the rear or side yard at least 20 ft from neighboring homes, with a maximum coop size of 200 sq ft and 8 ft height; Glendale's own application of this was not separately confirmed.
coop_rules: Poultry must be contained within a fence, corral or coop; manure, feed and water sanitation rules apply under state law.
zoning_notes: Glendale's pre-2024 zoning code allowed chicken-keeping only in A-1, RR-90, RR-45, SR-30, SR-17 and SR-12 zones; Arizona's 2024 state law (A.R.S. 9-462.12, HB 2325) now overrides that and guarantees up to 6 hens on any qualifying single-family lot regardless of zone.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.
code_section: A.R.S. 9-462.12 (state law); city zoning code chicken provisions predate this

sources.name: Glendale Star, New law to allow Arizonans to have backyard chickens
Cronkite News, Glendale move for backyard chickens

research_notes: Applying Arizona's 2024 state preemption law (confirmed high-confidence at the state level) to Glendale; no official Glendale city page updating its own code to match the 2024 state law was found, and the older city zoning-only rule is documented mainly in a 2016 Cronkite News piece. Confidence is medium because the city's own current code text was not read directly.
